title: Accordion
summary: A native disclosure group with single- or multi-open behavior, roving header shortcuts, and disabled-panel support.
overview: A dependency-free accordion based on details and summary, so disclosure semantics and basic interaction survive without JavaScript. Enhancement adds group isolation, arrow-key header navigation, control methods, and lifecycle cleanup.

component.useWhen: Use an accordion to let people scan several related headings and reveal concise supporting content in place.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid it when most content must be compared at once, when sections are unrelated, or when hidden content contains critical information.

examples.title: Single-open accordion
examples.description: Open each panel, then use Arrow keys, Home, and End while a summary is focused. Only one answer remains open.

variants.title: Multiple open panels
variants.summary: Independent disclosure panels with expand-all and collapse-all controls for comparison-heavy content.
variants.useWhen: Use multiple-open behavior when people benefit from comparing two or more short sections at the same time.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid global controls for a long set whose fully expanded content would become difficult to scan.
customization: Omitting the details name attribute makes each native disclosure independent.
expandAll() and collapseAll() expose the same behavior used by the demo controls.
Arrow-key navigation remains scoped to the summary elements inside this accordion.

variants.title: Disabled panel
variants.summary: A sequential accordion that marks an unavailable disclosure, removes it from keyboard order, and blocks activation.
variants.useWhen: Use a disabled panel only when a visible sequence must explain a later step that is not available yet.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid disabled disclosures in ordinary FAQs; omit unavailable content or explain the prerequisite next to an enabled action.
customization: aria-disabled communicates the state while the controller blocks pointer activation and removes the summary from sequential focus.
The muted text, unavailable cursor, and dash indicator communicate the state without color alone.

anatomy.name: Accordion group
anatomy.description: A bounded set of related disclosure items with one shared visual surface.

anatomy.name: Disclosure item
anatomy.description: A native details element that owns one summary and one content panel.

anatomy.name: Summary
anatomy.description: The visible, keyboard-operable heading that toggles its associated panel.

anatomy.name: Indicator
anatomy.description: A decorative plus or minus that mirrors the native open state.

anatomy.name: Panel
anatomy.description: Concise supporting content revealed by its summary.

tokens.name: --accordion-accent-text
tokens.description: Text used when an emphasized control uses the accent.

accessibility: Native details and summary provide disclosure semantics and Enter/Space activation without custom ARIA.
Arrow Down, Arrow Up, Home, and End move focus among summaries as an optional enhancement.
Do not place buttons, links, inputs, or other interactive controls inside summary.
The indicator is generated content and never carries the only accessible label.
Disabled summaries use aria-disabled, leave the tab sequence, reject pointer activation, and are skipped by arrow navigation.
Visible focus and open state use outline, text symbols, and shape rather than color alone.
component.responsive: The surface fills the available width up to 42rem. At 32rem and below, the preview and panel padding tighten to preserve readable content without horizontal scrolling.
limitations: The native exclusive details name behavior requires a current browser; older browsers may allow more than one default panel to remain open.
Panel content is present in the DOM even while collapsed; this recipe does not lazy-load expensive content.
The disabled variant depends on JavaScript because summary has no native disabled attribute.
Open and close motion uses the native details content pseudo-element in browsers that support it; older browsers retain immediate native disclosure behavior.

provenance.label: Cross-library accordion behavior study
provenance.note: Original native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no library source is copied.
